references.professionalService: Helps a client or reviewer understand how an authored timber-house assembly relates to a walkable finished space.
references.serviceOutcome: An annotated component assembly becomes one continuous interior visit through the east threshold, living area and loft.
references.decisionValue: Supports discussion of assembly intent and spatial relationships in this study; it does not certify a construction sequence or structural specification.

references.professionalService: Helps a client or design reviewer understand how the floor, four elevations and ceiling of this authored kitchen relate to the enclosed room and its usable interior.
references.serviceOutcome: A developed room drawing folds around its real pictured floor, then a camera passes through the same door to inspect kitchen and window bench.
references.decisionValue: Supports discussion of spatial relationships and design intent in this study; printed dimensions, north and finish codes are authored demo content, not certified project data.

references.professionalService: Explains the vertical organization and level-three workspace of one authored multilevel timber building to a client or design reviewer.
references.serviceOutcome: An exploded building stacks from the ground upward, holds an upper-level gap to reveal the studio, then lowers the overhead plate as the camera traverses that same floor.
references.decisionValue: Clarifies spatial relationship between levels and occupied studio in this study; the apparent weekly construction sequence, stretched core and roof garden are authored demo claims rather than Rubik project facts.

references.professionalService: Helps an architect explain how a section drawing relates to occupied rooms, vertical movement and the garden-facing exterior of the same house.
references.serviceOutcome: A technical section gains depth and material, the viewer follows a continuous route through upper, entrance and garden levels, then returns to the original sheet.
references.decisionValue: Supports discussion of spatial organization and the relationship between a drawing and lived rooms. The authored house, furniture, sun dates and CTA are donor-specific claims, not transferable Rubik project facts.

references.professionalService: Helps an architect explain what rooms and vertical movement lie behind one hillside section drawing while keeping the cut readable as perspective, material and light are introduced.
references.serviceOutcome: One technical 1:100 section opens its lens without losing the cut, gains material and sunlight, visits stair/rooms/pool and returns to a material section before editorial service copy.
references.decisionValue: Supports discussion of level relationships, circulation, daylight and the link between a technical cut and occupied space. The specific house, site and project facts are authored donor content.

references.professionalService: Helps an architect explain how one hillside house connects its street, bedroom and garden levels through the stair while retaining the section as the common spatial reference.
references.serviceOutcome: A measured section gains depth and material, the camera descends from street kitchen through bedroom and living levels to the pool, then returns to the whole material section.
references.decisionValue: Supports discussion of circulation, level relationships, daylight and the route from street to garden. The house and level numbers are donor-authored examples.

references.professionalService: Explains a proposed construction sequence for one hillside house through an aligned programme, staged 3D site and fixed-week drawings.
references.serviceOutcome: The visitor sees excavation through structure, props, finishes and handover while a week indicator and programme move together, then the completed house returns to drawing 06 on the six-view sheet.
references.decisionValue: Useful for discussing intended construction order and temporary works only as an illustration. The 38-week durations and stage assignments are authored demo content, not a calculated schedule or actual execution record.

references.professionalService: Communicates an example 14-week timber-house construction sequence with an aligned programme and visual build.
references.serviceOutcome: A viewer can scrub the same authored week across Gantt rows, staged house pieces and an automatic five-stop handover tour.
references.decisionValue: Useful for discussing illustrative sequence and spatial consequences; its dates, durations, completion percentages and critical-path label are not verified planning or execution facts.

references.professionalService: Explains how one planned building emerges from a foundation drawing and construction programme on its actual site footprint.
references.serviceOutcome: A viewer follows the same authored week across printed plan, programme, staged geometry and camera, ending with the complete house over its drawing.
references.decisionValue: Useful for spatial explanation of an illustrative build sequence; the printed dates, phase membership and completion percentages are fixed demo data, not verified project planning or execution.

references.professionalService: Shows an illustrative construction sequence from a site-camera viewpoint while connecting visible build stages to a programme, a changing daylight clock and a final interior walk-through.
references.serviceOutcome: A viewer can see how the same timber house rises over 14 authored weeks, approach it after handover and inspect five interior locations.
references.decisionValue: Useful for communicating spatial consequences and a possible site presentation; the dates, clock, phase progress and CRITICAL PATH are synthetic demo displays, not actual site telemetry or certified work.

references.professionalService: Lets an architect explain to a client how one physical 1:100 study model relates to the spatial scale and lived rooms of the proposed house.
references.serviceOutcome: The same house and contoured site move from card and desk into a materialized exterior/interior visit, reveal a nested model in the study, and return to the original card presentation.
references.decisionValue: Can clarify proportion, site relation and room experience during design discussion. The donor studio CTA and authored house are not evidence of a Rubik project or a verified construction outcome.

references.professionalService: Let an architect or client read one drawn street elevation as a sunlit, materialized house and follow its front door through actual room relationships to the rear courtyard.
references.serviceOutcome: The same townhouse drawing gains depth, brick and physically related shadow; a reversible camera route tests entry, parlour, atrium and garden continuity.
references.decisionValue: Can clarify facade depth, orientation, shadow and room sequence in project review. Donor address, area, status and booking call to action are authored copy, not verified Rubik project facts.

references.professionalService: Let a developer, architect or buyer compare six distinct townhouse plots in one street composition, identify the available plot 04 and inspect its entrance and key rooms.
references.serviceOutcome: The same numbered row changes from drawing to materialized street while plot 04 stays identified; the route enters its show house and ends in the atrium facing its garden.
references.decisionValue: Clarifies repeated-versus-varied facade relation and the spatial experience behind one selected plot. Donor sold/reserved/available states, bedroom count, area and reservation CTA are authored, not verified Rubik facts.

references.professionalService: Let an architect, material supplier or client inspect how a proposed facade bond and physically projecting headers read at drawing scale, under normal/raking sun and at human approach scale.
references.serviceOutcome: A 1:20 ink facade becomes a material wall; the same header lattice casts changing real shadows, is inspected close up and remains continuous through the porch into the hall.
references.decisionValue: Can support material/relief discussion and sample-panel evaluation. Kiln & Course, KC-06, 60 mm headers, mortar and order CTA are invented donor specifications, not verified Rubik material/project facts.
